name: Molt EVM
rootCause: Molt EVM, an experimental self-replicating ERC-20 token protocol on Base, was exploited due to a weak access control flaw. The attacker deployed a malicious contract to bypass the onlySpawnerToken modifier, minted large amounts of tokens via mintFromSpawner(), and dumped them through liquidity pools for profit.

descriptions.text: Molt EVM, an experimental self-replicating ERC-20 token protocol on Base, was exploited due to a weak access control flaw. The attacker deployed a malicious contract to bypass the onlySpawnerToken modifier, minted large amounts of tokens via mintFromSpawner(), and dumped them through liquidity pools for profit.

On 7 March 2026, Molt EVM on Base was exploited due to a flawed access control on the mintFromSpawner function, enabling an attacker to mint 100 million mEVM tokens and drain liquidity pools of ~50 WETH. Total losses were around $127,000. The onlySpawnerToken modifier failed to properly restrict mintFromSpawner: it allowed any contract whose initialized() function returns true to mint unlimited tokens, with no whitelist, role, or address check.
